title: Two exclusions permit exact reciprocal fits in 36 selected same-sign worm response pairs
abstract: We tested how many response pairs must be excluded to fit reciprocal transfer with free positive cell gains. We linked the WT Randi signal atlas to two adult Witvliet anatomy maps. In 36 selected same-sign pairs with a direct anatomy link in either adult, exact magnitudes require two pair exclusions. Exhaustive enumeration found 12 minimum sets using seven distinct pairs. No pair occurs in all minimum sets. At an allowed change factor of 1.075 per response magnitude, one exclusion is needed and four choices work. At factor 1.1, none is needed. One additional opposite-sign pair needs exclusion if signs are fixed. Stricter q and occurrence filters each leave a one-exclusion mismatch. The 22-pair anatomy intersection has no cycles and fits exact same-sign magnitudes. These are conditional sensitivity results, not error detection or evidence of biological nonreciprocity. Selected pooled calcium means, free gains and anatomy from different animals limit inference. Code, aggregate results, a figure and pinned external retrieval steps support reproduction.

display.caption: Minimum same-sign pair exclusions and the number of minimum exclusion sets under assumed magnitude change factors. The scopes overlap. Opposite-sign pairs are counted separately in the report.

citations.reason: Uses its response selection and reciprocal transfer model; adds minimum pair exclusions and exhaustive repair enumeration.
Prior calibration-bound sensitivity test on the same data; the present study leaves gains unrestricted and varies pair exclusion.
